The core challenge is that binary outcomes contain less information than margins of victory, leading to multiple plausible ways to map noisy wins/losses onto latent team abilities. The proposed model treats each team's performance as a draw from a shared normal distribution, shrinking extreme estimates toward the mean. This addresses separation issues but introduces dependence across teams through shared variance parameters. The resulting posterior distribution involves an intractable high-dimensional integral, requiring numerical approximations that can alter relative team orders. Different quadrature methods, prior specifications, or handling of ties all produce distinct point estimators for the same observed data, demonstrating fundamental nonidentifiability.
